faq.q: Is bina a homeschool program or a school?
faq.a: A school. Your child has a class, a timetable, certified teachers and report cards — the same structure as an in-person school, delivered live online. Most state programs list us under online or nonpublic schooling rather than homeschool curriculum, and we tell you exactly which category applies in your state before you apply.

faq.q: What if my state approves me for less than the full amount?
faq.a: You pay the difference. We show you the number before you commit, and we offer quarterly and yearly plans plus $1,500 off per additional child, so the gap is a monthly figure you can plan around.

faq.q: What if my application is turned down, or the window has closed?
faq.a: You are not stuck with a school you never chose. Families join bina and pay directly while an application is pending, and we time your start around your funding date once it is confirmed. Nothing about enrolling forces you to wait for the state.

faq.q: My child is neurodivergent or has an IEP. Does that change anything?
faq.a: Often in your favor — several states fund more per child for special needs. On our side, small classes and a Family Success team are the whole point; parents of neurodivergent children are a large share of our families, and they say so in the reviews on this page.

faq.q: Can I use ESA money for bina alongside other things?
faq.a: That depends on your state's rules and your award, not on us. Tuition for an online school is an approved category in the states listed here; whether there is room left over for other purchases is a question for your state's handbook, and we will point you at the exact page.

Your ESA covers about $7,000–$8,000 a year. You top up the rest.

faq.q: Is bina an approved Arizona ESA school?
faq.a: Yes. bina has been an approved school on ClassWallet since November 2024, and the Arizona Department of Education confirmed our registration in June 2026.

faq.q: Does the ESA cover all of bina's tuition?
faq.a: It covers most of it. On the yearly plan, families usually top up about $231–$314 a month, depending on their award.

faq.q: Is there an application deadline?
faq.a: Arizona accepts applications all year. The date you sign your ESA agreement sets which quarter your funding starts, so applying earlier means funding starts sooner.

faq.q: How long does approval take?
faq.a: Up to 45 days after you apply, according to the Arizona Department of Education.

faq.q: How does bina get paid?
faq.a: We send you an invoice. You create an order in ClassWallet, the state reviews it and pays bina directly, usually within about a week.

faq.q: Will someone help me with the application?
faq.a: Yes. Monet and Jose from our admissions team guide you through every step, from the application to your first payment.

faq.q: Do you offer a sibling discount?
faq.a: Yes. Each additional child gets $1,500 off tuition.

faq.q: My child is in public school now. Can we still apply?
faq.a: Yes. Your child can apply while in public school and studies with bina once your ESA is active.

faq.q: What if my child has an IEP or 504 plan?
faq.a: Arizona may give a larger award for children with qualifying needs, which can lower your top-up. We'll go through your numbers with you.

faq.q: Is bina responsible for this program?
faq.a: The Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) is run by the state of Arizona, not by bina. Program amounts, eligibility and deadlines are subject to change. Always confirm with the official program site before you rely on a number here.

states.h1: Utah families can use Utah Fits All funds toward a bina education
gate: bina is an approved Utah Fits All provider

faq.q: The window is closed. Is there any point talking to you now?
faq.a: Yes — that is exactly when it helps. The next window is Mar 1 – May 1, 2027, awards are limited, and the families who get funded are the ones who applied in the first days with clean paperwork. We get you ready for it, and plenty of families start at bina in the meantime and pay directly.

faq.q: Are Utah Fits All awards guaranteed if I qualify?
faq.a: No. Every Utah K–12 family is eligible, but the money runs out — awards are announced in mid-June and you accept by the end of June. We plan your bina start around your notification date rather than assuming the award, so a no from the state never leaves you without a school.

faq.q: $8,000 against $10,769 — what is left for me?
faq.a: About $230 a month, before $1,500 off for each additional child. Utah Fits All is the largest base award of the five states on this site.

faq.q: Does bina being outside Utah — or outside the US — disqualify us?
faq.a: No. Utah's statute explicitly contemplates a private school not physically located in Utah, and you spend the scholarship through the Odyssey marketplace where bina is a provider.

gate: bina tuition qualifies for the credit
Up to $5,000 per child ($7,500 for special needs)
Paid to you — as a refund or an advance

faq.q: Does Idaho pay bina, or pay me?
faq.a: You. This one is a tax credit, not a school account — you pay bina, submit the receipts, and Idaho returns up to $5,000 per child as a refundable credit or an advance payment. We give you the itemized invoice, enrollment letter and accreditation details every time you need them.

faq.q: So I have to fund the whole year myself first?
faq.a: You fund it and claim it back — and you can apply for the advance payment rather than waiting for a refund. We have quarterly and yearly plans, and $1,500 off per additional child, so the cash-flow shape is something we work out with you on the call.

faq.q: Both 2026 windows closed. Have we missed it?
faq.a: For 2026, yes. The next window is Jan 15 – Mar 15, 2027. Because the claim is built on receipts, starting at bina now does not cost you eligibility — it gives you the receipts. It is first come, first served, so being documented and ready in January matters more in Idaho than anywhere else.

faq.q: Who gets priority in 2027?
faq.a: Families who received the credit the year before, then households at or below 300% of the federal poverty level, then everyone else in the order applications arrive.

faq.q: Up to $5,000 — what is my real cost?
faq.a: About $480 a month net of the credit, before $1,500 off for each additional child. A child with a disability qualifies for up to $7,500, which brings it down further.

faq.q: You don't know the 2027 dates. Why should I trust the rest of this page?
faq.a: Because we would rather say we don't know than guess. The Wyoming Department of Education has not announced the 2027–28 window; for 2026–27 it opened 9 a.m. on Jul 6 and ran to the end of July, so plan for early July 2027. Tell us you're in Wyoming and you will hear from us the day it is published — before the window, not after it closes.

faq.q: Is bina actually in Wyoming's provider list?
faq.a: Yes — bina is an approved Education Service Provider and you spend the scholarship through Odyssey. Wyoming's own guidance says a certified ESP does not need to be located in Wyoming and can provide virtual services from anywhere.

faq.q: $7,000 against $10,769 — what do I pay?
faq.a: About $315 a month, before $1,500 off for each additional child. Renewing families also get $1,750 in rollover funds, which reduces it further in year two.

faq.q: When does the money actually arrive?
faq.a: Wyoming verifies eligibility within about a month of the window closing and the $7,000 lands in your Odyssey account by September 1. We time your bina start around that date.

faq.q: The window is closed and school has started. What now?
faq.a: Families enroll and pay directly, and we line the funding up for the next cycle. Nothing about starting at bina now makes the next application harder — it makes it easier, because you already have an enrolled child and a paper trail.

states.h1: New Hampshire families can use EFA funds toward a bina education

faq.q: I thought the EFA had an income limit.
faq.a: It did — until 2025, when SB 295 removed the 350% federal-poverty-level cap. Every New Hampshire K–12 family is now eligible. Enrollment is capped statewide at 12,500 students, so early is better, but your income is no longer the question.

faq.q: Can we apply mid-year?
faq.a: Yes. The EFA is rolling all year. Apply and be verified by Jul 15 for a full award for the coming year; after that you can still get a prorated award for the year already underway, right through the end of February.

faq.q: When does the money arrive, and does it match how bina bills?
faq.a: Funds land in your ClassWallet account in four installments — September, November, January and April. That lines up with how bina bills, so you are not asked for money the state hasn't sent yet.

faq.q: About $3,800–$5,800 against $10,769 — what is my share?
faq.a: About $414–$581 a month, before $1,500 off for each additional child. We put your exact figure in writing before you commit.

faq.q: How long does a decision take?
faq.a: About 30 days, or up to two months if the state asks for more documents — which is why we suggest talking to us first and applying with your bina numbers and paperwork already in hand.

howEsa.title: The Hope Scholarship in plain words
howEsa.body: The Hope Scholarship is West Virginia's Education Savings Account, run by the West Virginia State Treasurer's Office. When your child is approved and your Notice of Intent is on file, the state puts money into a Hope account for your child's education, a quarter of the award at a time (by August 15, October 15, January 15 and April 15). You spend it on approved expenses, including tuition at an online school like bina, and the money goes from your account to the school, not to you.

qualifies.title: Can your family use the Hope Scholarship?

items.v: Your child lives in West Virginia and stays a resident while in the program.
Your child is enrolled in, or eligible to enroll in, a West Virginia public school from kindergarten to grade 12. bina teaches from Pre-K to Grade 10. Pre-K isn't covered by the Hope Scholarship.
Your child is at least 5 before July 1.
From 2026–27, every West Virginia K–12 student can apply, including children already in private school or homeschool.
Your child isn't enrolled full time in a public school.

Applications are open all year, and the date you apply sets your first-year award. For 2026–27: 50% of the award until November 30, 2026, and 25% from December 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027. After February 28, applications count toward the 2027–28 school year.

2.d: Create an account at hopescholarshipwv.gov and complete the application for each child. Upload your child's state-issued birth certificate and proof of West Virginia residency. If your child has attended a West Virginia public school, add their WVEIS number (it's on their report card).

3.d: Once your application shows "Eligible", file a Notice of Intent with your county board of education. You only file it once, and your account is funded only after it's on file.

4.d: Choose your start date and sign your agreement with bina for the remaining balance. If your child is enrolled full time in a public school, withdraw them before they start at bina.

5.t: Pay bina from your Hope account
5.d: Funds arrive each quarter. We send you an invoice, you pay bina from your Hope account, and you pay the difference.

faq.q: Is bina approved for the Hope Scholarship?
faq.a: Yes. bina is approved for West Virginia's Hope Scholarship, so you can use your Hope funds toward bina tuition.

faq.q: Does the Hope Scholarship cover all of bina's tuition?
faq.a: It covers about half. With the full award, families on the yearly plan top up about $444 a month.

faq.q: When can I apply?
faq.a: Applications are open all year, and the date you apply sets your first-year award. If you apply by November 30, 2026, you receive 50% of the 2026–27 award, and from December 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027, you receive 25%. From the next school year, you receive the full award.

faq.q: What is a Notice of Intent?
faq.a: A form you file with your county board of education once your application shows "Eligible". You file it once, and your Hope account is funded only after it's on file.

faq.q: When does the money arrive?
faq.a: The state adds a quarter of the award to your account by August 15, October 15, January 15 and April 15.

faq.q: My child is in public school now. Can we still apply?
faq.a: Yes. Every West Virginia K–12 student can apply. Your child can't stay enrolled full time in a public school while using Hope funds, so they move to bina once you're ready to start.

faq.q: Is there anything I need to do each year?
faq.a: Yes. Confirm your child's place in the program between January 5 and June 15 each year. We send you new paperwork for it.

faq.q: Will someone help me with the application?
faq.a: Yes. Our financial aid team guides you through every step, from the application to your first payment.

faq.q: Do you offer a sibling discount?
faq.a: Yes. Each additional child gets $1,500 off tuition.

faq.q: Is bina responsible for this program?
faq.a: The Hope Scholarship is run by the state of West Virginia, not by bina. Program amounts, eligibility and deadlines are subject to change. Always confirm with the official program site before you rely on a number here.
